significance_caveat: At n=5 the two-sided exact sign test cannot return below 0.0625, so NO five-fold dataset can support a significance claim about the sign of its mean. alabama (t p=0.0125), georgia (t p=0.0093) and california (t p=0.0478) all reject by t-test, but their sign tests are 0.0625, 0.0625 and 0.3750. Report consistent tendencies, never significance. Equivalence within +/-0.05 by TOST is the claim that survives, and it holds everywhere.
drift_caveat: alabama (5/5 negative, t p=0.0058) and georgia (5/5, t p=0.0470) lean negative, but the exact sign test gives 0.0625 for both, ITS FLOOR AT n=5 -- the same footing as the positive-mean claim this record declines to call significant, so the drift is not called significant either. california 4/5 (t p=0.2403), texas 3/5 positive-leaning (t p=0.5346), istanbul 2/5 (t p=0.9327). Florida, with 60 independent series, is flat (t p=0.7108, 29/60) and is the only estimate with enough units to settle the question.
